learning_objectives: Explain what tokens are, how tokenization works, and why they matter for LLM performance, cost, and context management.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Large Language Models (**LLMs**)

slides.title: Title Slide
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on Understanding **Tokens** and **Tokenization**.
slides.image_prompt: Title Slide: 'Understanding Tokens and Tokenization' with a stylized graphic of text breaking into small pieces.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn about:
What **tokens** are.
How **tokenization** works.
Why **tokens** are important for **LLMs**.
slides.image_prompt: Learning Objectives Slide: List of objectives.

slides.title: Pre-requisites
slides.narration: To follow this tutorial, you should have a basic understanding of **Large Language Models**, or **LLMs**.
slides.image_prompt: Pre-requisite Slide: Text 'Basic understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs)'.

slides.title: Introduction to Tokens
content: LLMs don't read words like humans.
slides.narration:
Welcome to a fundamental concept.
**LLMs** are very smart.
But they do not read words like humans.
They read **tokens** instead.
slides.image_prompt: Abstract visual representing an **LLM** processing text, showing 'words' transforming into smaller 'token' blocks.

slides.title: What is a Tokenizer?
content: A Tokenizer splits raw text into sub-word pieces.
These pieces are what the model understands.
slides.narration:
So, what are **tokens**?
Think of them as small pieces of text.
A **Tokenizer** is like a special dictionary.
It splits raw text into these pieces.
The **LLM** understands these pieces.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic showing raw text 'Hello world!' entering a 'Tokenizer' box and coming out as segmented pieces: ['Hello'][' ']['world']['!'].

slides.title: Token Examples
content: Simple words can be one token (e.g., 'The').
Complex words can be multiple tokens (e.g., 'Tokenization' -> 'Token', 'iz', 'ation').
slides.narration:
Let's see an example.
A simple word like 'The' might be one **token**.
But a complex word like '**Tokenization**' is different.
It might be broken into three **tokens**.
Like '**Token**', '**iz**', and '**ation**'.

slides.title: Why Do Tokens Matter?
content: Tokens impact Context Windows, Cost, and Chunking.
slides.narration:
Why should you care about **tokens**?
They are very important.
Let's see why.
slides.image_prompt: Question mark over a pile of various token blocks, emphasizing importance.

slides.title: Tokens and Context Windows
content: LLM's 'short-term memory' (Context Window) is measured in tokens.
This is a hard limit on how much context an LLM can process.
slides.narration:
First, consider **Context Windows**.
This is an **LLM**'s short-term memory.
It has a fixed limit.
This limit is measured in **tokens**.
For example, 8,192 **tokens**.
This is a hard limit.
It controls the context you send.
This includes your **prompt** and documents.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic showing a 'window' with a fixed number of token blocks inside, labeled 'Context Window Limit: 8,192 tokens'.

slides.title: Tokens and Cost
content: Fewer tokens lead to lower costs (e.g., GraphRAG reduced tokens by 26-97%).
slides.narration:
Next, think about cost.
**API** providers charge per **token**.
Fewer **tokens** mean lower costs.
An efficient **RAG** system uses fewer **tokens**.
This makes your projects much cheaper.
**GraphRAG** used 26% to 97% fewer **tokens**.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic showing a stack of tokens with a large dollar sign, then a smaller stack of tokens with a smaller dollar sign, illustrating cost reduction.

slides.title: Tokens and Chunking
content: When chunking documents, tokens help define pieces.
These pieces must fit within the Context Window.
slides.narration:
Finally, consider **chunking**.
When we **chunk** documents, we break them up.
These small pieces must fit.
They fit into the **LLM**'s **Context Window**.
**Tokens** help us define these chunks.
This ensures efficient processing.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic showing a long document being broken into smaller, token-sized chunks, with arrows pointing into a Context Window.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
With this, we come to the end of this tutorial.
Let us summarise.
We learned what **tokens** are.
We saw how a **Tokenizer** works.
And we understood why **tokens** are crucial for **LLMs**.
slides.image_prompt: Summary Slide: Recap of key points about tokens, tokenization, and their importance.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
As an assignment, please do the following.
Find an online **tokenizer** tool.
Enter a long sentence or a short paragraph.
Observe how it breaks the text into **tokens**.
Notice differences in common words versus complex ones.
